text:
alex: hi all, new hire here. followed the getting-started doc and ran `rwd-kube login` but the `redwood-` contexts didn't show up in my `kubectl config get-contexts`. i'm on macOS and i think my KUBECONFIG might be weird. any quick checks? :wave:
sophia: welcome alex! first check `echo $KUBECONFIG` and `ls -l $HOME/.kube`. sometimes we have a legacy `~/.kube/config.local` floating around.
alex: `echo $KUBECONFIG` prints `/Users/alex/.kube/config.local` and `ls -l` shows both `config` and `config.local` (config is a symlink to config.local).
sophia: aha. `rwd-kube` by default writes to `~/.kube/config` and will merge, but if you have KUBECONFIG set it can change kubectl lookup order. try `kubectl config get-contexts --kubeconfig=$HOME/.kube/config` to see what's actually in the file.
alex: running that shows the new contexts:```
CURRENT  NAME                          CLUSTER           AUTHINFO
         redwood-dev-gke-02-alex       gke-redwood-02    alex@okta
         redwood-staging-gke-01-alex   gke-redwood-01    alex@okta
*        minikube                      minikube          minikube
```
but `kubectl config get-contexts` (without --kubeconfig) still only shows minikube.
sophia: that's because `kubectl` will interpret KUBECONFIG env var as a colon-separated list and use that instead of `~/.kube/config`. looks like your shell is exporting the old path. run `unset KUBECONFIG` and then `kubectl config get-contexts` again.
alex: i unset and now i see the redwood contexts! thanks. i tried to `kubectl use-context redwood-dev-gke-02-alex` but then got `error: context "redwood-dev-gke-02-alex" does not exist` when i re-opened a new terminal.
sophia: did you also add the merge to your default `~/.kube/config`? `rwd-kube login` should have updated it. maybe your shells are using a cached kubeconfig via the `KUBECONFIG` env var in your .zshrc. check for any lines referencing kubeconfig in your shell rc.
alex: oh yeah i had `export KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/config.local` in my .zshrc from an old setup. removing that and restarting terminal fixed it.
k8s-admin: quick note: we prefer team-level group bindings rather than individual user RBAC for new hires. alex, do you need namespace access yet or just dev cluster read-only?
alex: read-only for now, eventually will need edit in `infra-platform-dev`.
k8s-admin: created a ClusterRoleBinding for `okta:team-infra-platform` to `view` on dev clusters. if you need `edit` in infra ns, ping with the env and team and we'll apply the RoleBinding.
oncall-bot: kubeconfig refresh token for user alex will expire in 23h 58m (reminder: run `rwd-kube login` to refresh).
alex: sweet, everything's working now. added a note in my onboarding checklist to check for stray KUBECONFIG exports. thanks! :tada:
